The memory prompt forbids calling or assuming any external database.
enum_values: outcome: no results_history -> 'there are no stored results in this session yet'
outcome: named id not found -> "I couldn't find that in this session"
planner alias: memory_lookup and ask_about_last_results are functionally identical, only the reported tool name differs

capabilities.name: Select WHICH prior result bundle a follow-up refers to
capabilities.description: Three layers: the parser picks target_result_id from the visible window (newest by default, oldest for 'the first search'/'originally'/'earliest', or the bundle whose query mentions a named entity); when it cannot, resolve_bundle_for_recall scores every bundle by significant-word overlap so 'the first search' does not silently resolve to the newest; the planner variant additionally accepts explicit metadata keys.
enum_values: target_result_id = null + notes 'bundle not in visible window — memory agent should look it up by content'
recall word pattern \b[\w.-]{2,}\b preserves dots/dashes so D.SEQ, NDMA, MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB survive
planner metadata bundle-id keys: target_result_id, refers_to_result_id, result_id, bundle_id
planner metadata query keys: target_query, prior_query, original_query, refers_to_query
planner latest-bundle trigger tokens: 'last result', 'latest result', 'previous result', 'those results', 'that search'

capabilities.name: Compute the follow-up answer with sandboxed generated Python
capabilities.description: The fast path: pick the best JSON payload out of the prior bundle, profile its shape, ask the memory_coder for a short Python snippet, execute it in an AST-validated subset under a 3-second SIGALRM, save a timestamped artifact, and have the chatter phrase the computed result. The prompt mandates exact field comparison over substring scans (a substring 'SHA' matched URL fragments inside HTML-wrapped UIDs) and prefers 'I do not have that field' over guessing.
enum_values: pre-bound names: data, rows, re, json, strip_html, result
allowed builtins: len, str, int, float, bool, list, dict, set, tuple, sorted, sum, min, max, any, all, enumerate, range, isinstance
allowed exception classes: Exception, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError
allowed methods: get, items, keys, values, append, extend, add, update, lower, upper, strip, split, replace, startswith, endswith, isdigit, join
allowed re methods: search, match, fullmatch, findall, sub
allowed control flow: if/elif/else, for, comprehensions, try/except
blocked AST nodes: Import, ImportFrom, FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef, ClassDef, Lambda, With, AsyncWith, Delete, Global, Nonlocal, Raise, While, Await, Yield, YieldFrom
blocked names: eval, exec, compile, open, __import__, globals, locals, vars, dir, help, input, print
blocked: any dunder attribute access or dunder method call
blocked: dynamic calls (target neither Name nor Attribute)
result carries: count, examples, field_used, match_strategy
payload priority: bundle memory_payload > saved artifacts (api 0 > graph 1 > report 2 > other 5 > plan debug 9) > inline planner rows/reply > graph_result/api_result_full/api_result_slim

capabilities.name: Schema-agnostic JSON profiling for the follow-up prompt
capabilities.description: Summarises an arbitrary result into a bounded skeleton, a list of likely record arrays with their JSON paths, and a field_index classifying each row field as categorical or free_text with distinct-value examples. The field_index is what lets the coder prefer exact equality on a real field over a substring scan — the difference between counting 'male' correctly and matching 'female' too. Parses json_metadata whether it arrives as a dict or a JSON string.
enum_values: output: {root_type, skeleton, record_arrays:[{path, length, examples}], field_index:{row_top_level, row_json_metadata, rows_scanned, note}}

capabilities.name: Fallback: answer the follow-up by feeding the saved result files to the model
capabilities.description: When the code path fails at any stage (payload load, coder call, sandbox execution) this loads every saved artifact of the bundle as text (recursively HTML-stripped; non-JSON files fall back to raw content) and asks the question against that content only. On double failure it returns a degraded message that still reports the prior record count and names both errors.

capabilities.name: Inject prior bundles and chat history into the prompt

capabilities.name: Reuse the last result set by reference ('those samples')

When more bundles exist it appends an explicit NOTE telling the parser to infer from CHAT_HISTORY instead. Returns 'No prior results in this session.' when empty.

capabilities.name: Answering a follow-up from a stored bundle (memory_coder fast path + legacy fallback)
capabilities.description: memory_agent_answer profiles the bundle's JSON, has memory_coder generate a guarded Python extraction snippet, executes it locally, writes a uniquely-named artifact (memory_coder_bundle_<bid>_<UTC-ts>.json) and has the chatter phrase the computed result under 'MODE: memory_computed'. capabilities.name: resolve_bundle_for_recall — picking WHICH prior bundle a memory question is about
capabilities.description: Used when the parser sets target_result_id=null. Scores every bundle in results_history by significant-word overlap between the current question and the bundle's stored user_query (stopword list strips ~90 common words plus NExtSEEK chrome; dots/dashes preserved so 'D.SEQ' and 'MUS-200901ENG-23-PUB' survive). Ties break toward recency; falls back to the most recent bundle when no overlap; returns None only when history is empty.

capabilities.name: Monotonic bundle ids that survive a lost append
capabilities.description: _next_bundle_id allocates from a separate BUNDLE_SEQ_KEY counter rather than len(results_history)+1, because the old derivation collided whenever an append did not survive (concurrent writers on a stale JSON snapshot, a trim, a failed save) and a later 'what were those results?' then resolved to a different question's bundle.

ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE). Values are JSON-encoded. Used by the CLI/Streamlit/MCP surfaces; inside Django the DictSessionAdapter replaces it entirely.

capabilities.name: Top-level parser route enum (7 values) and the single-path parser
capabilities.description: Every NS-engine turn is classified into exactly one of seven execution routes by the parser, which reads the question plus resolved entities, recent bundles, chat history, the REST endpoint catalog and the graph schema, and emits a ParserPlan naming ONE path plus the filters and endpoint that path needs. The field defaults to 'unsupported', so a failure to route is a refusal, not a random search.
enum_values: ParserPlan fields: mode, target_endpoint, intent_summary, report_mode, report_type, resolved, filters, target_result_id, endpoint_candidates, notes, previous_api_plan, previous_user_query, metadata

capabilities.name: Select (or rank) the target REST endpoint for a search turn
capabilities.description: When the parser picks new_search or refine_last_search it must also name one endpoint from the enriched catalog, choosing the most specific match and treating advanced_search as a last-resort catch-all. It may instead emit ranked endpoint_candidates {endpoint, rationale, confidence}; the field is a permissive union so a model emitting plain strings still validates. An optional semantic shortlist trims the catalog handed to the prompt, off by default and byte-identical when off.
enum_values: POST /nextseek_api/admin/samples/retrieve/ — full metadata + full lineage for explicit UIDs (body field must be 'identifiers'); output_format='excel' gives a workbook
GET /nextseek_api/assays/ — list all assays (titles, types, technologies)
GET /nextseek_api/sample-tree/{uid}/tree/ — bidirectional lineage tree around ONE UID
GET /nextseek_api/sample_types/ — all sample type schema definitions
POST /nextseek_api/sample_types/get_parents/parents_by_child_types/ — parents having derived samples of ALL specified child types
POST /nextseek_api/samples/advanced_search/ — broad attribute/keyword/free-text sample search, paginated
GET /nextseek_api/sops/ — list SOPs/protocols with attachment metadata
rule: advanced_search is the catch-all, used only when no more targeted endpoint fits
semantic shortlist gated by SEMANTIC_ENDPOINTS_ENABLED (default False), dynamic cutoff ratio 0.7 / min_k 10 / max_k 80

capabilities.name: Compose a graph-scope × REST-attribute intersection plan
capabilities.description: When the parser finds both a structural (graph) candidate and an attribute (REST) candidate each covering part of the question, it builds a deterministic 2-step intersect plan: step 1 takes the structural UID scope with all free-text keywords stripped out, step 2 applies the attribute filters, and the executor intersects the UID sets. Skipped when candidate 0 is a high-confidence specialized endpoint, because forcing a graph intersect adds UID-format risk with no benefit.
enum_values: bail-out: candidate 0 is new_search on a non-advanced_search endpoint with confidence >= 0.80
requirement: top structural candidate mode == 'graph_query' and confidence >= 0.60
scope-only rewrite blanks filters['keywords'] and drops metadata['keyword_filter']

With no bundle_id every manifest field is None and nothing is written.
enum_values: output: {turn_id, bundle_id, total, row_count, columns, path, reply}

capabilities.name: _NS_PATTERNS: the exact NS keyword alternation

capabilities.description: Four branches: CC-only match -> container_cc; NS-only match -> nextseek_query; BOTH match -> container_cc only if a CC verb matches the FIRST whitespace token of the query, else nextseek_query; NEITHER matches -> nextseek_query (the cheap, deterministic default). The first-token test uses query.split()[0] guarded against an empty query.

capabilities.description: _heuristic returns only ROUTE_CC or ROUTE_NS, so with BAML unavailable the third outcome is unreachable and every off-topic question is answered by an engine instead of the canned refusal. A deliberate degradation, and the reason 'unrelated' coverage requires a live BAML router.

families.description: force_route precedence, sticky-CC and its exits, the per-turn request envelope.

groups.name: Route-override precedence in _decide_route

capabilities.name: Precedence ladder: force > pipeline > sticky > router
capabilities.description: _decide_route resolves in this order: (1) an explicit force (force_cc kwarg from the cc/query/async endpoint, or an admin's force_route) short-circuits before the router is called at all; (2) cc_router.decide() runs; (3) the pipeline_agent guard may redirect an NS-bound turn; (4) the sticky-CC guard may redirect an NS-bound turn. Guards 3 and 4 run AFTER the router deliberately, so an open wizard or a sticky chat can never capture a turn the model never saw.
enum_values: source: baml | heuristic (level 2, no guard fired)

capabilities.name: force_cc endpoint override (POST cc/query/async)
capabilities.description: The dedicated cc_query_async action calls _start_task(force_cc=True), which bypasses the router entirely for that turn. This is an endpoint-level force, NOT admin-gated (any authenticated user hitting that URL forces CC).

capabilities.name: Admin-only force_route: admin path
capabilities.description: force_route in {"ns","cc"} from an is_staff or is_superuser caller produces an immediate RouteDecision with source="forced" and reasoning="forced". "cc" also pins opus + the CC model id; "ns" carries model_class None / model_id None. force_route="auto" (and None) falls through to the router.

capabilities.name: Admin-only force_route: non-admin is silently ignored
capabilities.description: The server re-checks is_staff/is_superuser on every request and sets forced=None for non-admins, so their force_route falls through to the router with no error and no warning. Mirrors the use_prod admin gate. The frontend also hides the control, but the server gate is independent of the UI.

capabilities.name: A forced route can never be `unrelated`
capabilities.description: Both forced branches construct ROUTE_CC or ROUTE_NS directly and return before cc_router.decide() runs, so an explicitly forced turn always executes an engine instead of getting the canned out-of-scope refusal.

capabilities.name: pipeline_agent wizard gate (NS-bound turns only)
capabilities.description: When chat_nextseek.pipeline.agent.is_active(session) is true AND the router already chose nextseek_query, the decision is re-stamped source="pipeline" with reasoning 'pipeline_active; router said ns (<router reasoning>)' so confirm/tweak/launch turns reach pipeline_agent.handle_turn. A router choice of container_cc or unrelated is NOT overridden by an open wizard.

capabilities.name: Guards run after the router, never before (regression guard)
capabilities.description: Both the pipeline and sticky guards are explicitly ordered after cc_router.decide(). A prior implementation short-circuited the pipeline guard first, which made an open samplesheet build answer a plain sample search with 'searching the database isn't something I can do'. The order is documented as load-bearing in-source.

groups.name: Sticky-CC conversion and exit conditions

capabilities.name: NS -> CC sticky conversion
capabilities.description: When the router classifies a turn nextseek_query AND the most recent engine-running turn in this chat was container_cc with status completed, the decision is converted to container_cc with source="sticky", model_class opus, and reasoning 'sticky_cc; router said ns (<router reasoning>)'. Exists so a CC thread's follow-up ('Just the 4 week ones.') does not get yanked to NS and fail for want of an NS bundle to refine.

capabilities.name: Unrelated turns are transparent to the sticky scan
capabilities.description: _prev_route_was_cc walks the history backwards, CONTINUING past any turn whose router_choice is unrelated, and stops at the first engine-running turn it finds. Without this, one off-topic aside between two CC turns silently ended stickiness.

capabilities.name: A failed CC turn does not make the chat sticky
capabilities.description: The backwards scan stops at the FIRST engine-running turn regardless of status and returns True only when that turn is container_cc AND status=="completed". It deliberately does not keep looking for an older healthy CC turn, so a route that just broke cannot trap the conversation.

capabilities.name: Every way a chat exits sticky CC
capabilities.description: Four exits, all observable as source flipping away from "sticky": (a) a new chat (force_new or a new session_id — history is empty); (b) an admin force_route="ns" (level-1 force precedes the guard); (c) an intervening errored CC turn (RG-3.3); (d) history-window eviction — three consecutive unrelated turns push the CC turn out of the 5-turn window, an accepted consequence. A turn the router independently classifies container_cc still runs CC but with source "baml".
enum_values: exit: preceding CC turn ended status=error
exit: CC turn evicted past MAX_HISTORY_TURNS (5)

capabilities.name: Sticky never converts an `unrelated` decision
capabilities.description: The sticky condition requires decision.route == ROUTE_NS. An unrelated classification inside a sticky chat still returns the canned refusal rather than spinning up an Opus container for an out-of-scope question.

capabilities.name: Sticky inspection is crash-proof
capabilities.description: The _prev_route_was_cc call is wrapped in a bare except that logs and falls back to sticky=False, so malformed history can degrade routing but never fail the turn.

groups.name: Per-turn request envelope (QueryRequest)

capabilities.name: QueryRequest schema strictness and validation failure
capabilities.description: The single request model for POST /assistant/query/, /assistant/query/async/, /cc-assistant/query/async/ and /cc-assistant/cc/query/async/. ConfigDict(extra='forbid') means any unknown key is a hard 422 with the NExtSEEK errors envelope, not a silent ignore.
enum_values: fields: session_id, query, mode, force_new, use_prod, fresh_session, force_route, max_turn_length_s

capabilities.name: query (required, 1..32000 chars)
capabilities.description: The natural-language turn text. Required, min_length 1, max_length 32000. It is also what is stored on QueryTask.query and used as the auto-title fallback.

capabilities.name: mode (required free string; per-endpoint dispatch table)
capabilities.description: Required but NOT enum-constrained at the schema level; each endpoint interprets it differently. AssistantViewSet.query (SSE): 'plan' -> run_query_plan, anything else -> run_query. AssistantViewSet.query_async: 'plan' -> run_query_plan, 'pipeline' -> run_pipeline_launch, else run_query. CCAssistantViewSet._start_task on the NS route: 'plan' -> run_query_plan, else run_query — it has NO 'pipeline' branch, so mode='pipeline' on the routed endpoint silently runs the standard pipeline.
enum_values: standard (the frontend default / any unrecognised value)

capabilities.name: session_id (optional UUID, ownership-scoped)
capabilities.description: When supplied the session is fetched filtered by the requesting user; a miss is 404 'Session not found or you do not own it' (existence and ownership are indistinguishable on this path, unlike the session-detail endpoint which returns 403). When omitted, resolution falls to force_new / most-recent / auto-create.

capabilities.name: force_new (New-chat semantics)
capabilities.description: Only consulted when session_id is absent. True -> unconditionally create a new ChatSession; False -> reuse the caller's most recently updated session, auto-creating only if they have none. This is the frontend's 'New chat' button and the only user-facing way to reset routing history (and thus exit sticky CC).

capabilities.name: use_prod (admin-only prod ChatConfig switch)
capabilities.description: Selects settings.NEXTSEEK_CHAT_CONFIG_PROD only when ALL of: use_prod true, caller is is_staff/is_superuser, and a prod config was actually built in local_settings. Otherwise the default NEXTSEEK_CHAT_CONFIG. When the prod config is selected, the outbound Basic-auth credentials are ALSO swapped to the prod config's baked-in API_USER/API_PASS (the local session user does not exist on prod). On the routed endpoint the CC branch deliberately keeps the requesting user's credentials.
enum_values: fallback reasons: not admin | no NEXTSEEK_CHAT_CONFIG_PROD configured | use_prod false

capabilities.name: fresh_session (clean-room CC memory)
capabilities.description: CC-route only: skips the Step-1c cross-session memory layer (no per-session summarize, no rendered cross-session block in the mounted CLAUDE.md, no read-only transcripts mount). The within-chat NS/CC digest is still composed, and 1b resume inside this same chat still applies. No frontend control posts it — API/harness only.

capabilities.name: force_route (admin-only route override field)
capabilities.description: Literal['auto','ns','cc'] or None. Validation rejects any other string with 422 before routing is reached. Semantics and the admin gate are RG-2.3/RG-2.4; this capability is the field contract itself, including that the frontend omits it entirely when 'auto'.

capabilities.name: max_turn_length_s (admin-only per-turn wall clock, server-clamped)
capabilities.description: Optional int, ge=1 at the schema level. Non-admins have it forced to None before clamping. clamp_turn_timeout maps None/<=0 to _DEFAULT_TURN_TIMEOUT = min(NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_HARD_MAX) and otherwise clamps into [30, NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_HARD_MAX] (default hard max 180), so a UI override can never exceed the deployment ceiling. Affects the CC route only; surfaced as cc_turn_meta.turn_timeout_s.

groups.name: Carry memory across sessions and across containers

capabilities.name: Cross-session memory file merged into the agent's CLAUDE.md
capabilities.description: Categorized takeaways distilled from the user's most recent other sessions, plus read-only pointers to the raw transcripts. Every evidence quote is verified host-side; unverified items are kept and flagged, never dropped. Suppressed entirely by fresh_session.
enum_values: memory categories (render order): decision, preference, todo, artifact, context, fact
tool_use classifier kinds: bash, write, edit, read, skill, tool
header: '# Cross-session memory (auto-generated — do not edit)'

capabilities.name: Session distillation (BAML Summarize)
capabilities.description: Distills one Claude Code session transcript into a one-sentence gist plus at most 8 categorized takeaways, each citing an L<n> line range and a verbatim excerpt. Degrades to a deterministic fallback summary on ANY failure so a session is never left un-remembered.

capabilities.name: Celery backstop sweep for idle changed sessions
capabilities.description: A scheduled task that summarizes sessions the user never explicitly left, idle past a threshold and whose transcript fingerprint changed. Idempotent.

capabilities.name: Claude session resume across ephemeral containers
capabilities.description: Claude's own session id is sniffed off the stream, persisted, and passed back as --resume next turn; resume is skipped when the per-session store holds no transcript so it never resumes a session whose transcript is gone.

log line: 'cc: resume id present but store empty; starting fresh'

capabilities.name: Durable zstd transcript store with a recovery endpoint
capabilities.description: Each CC turn's complete session .jsonl is compressed into the database so it survives a wiped state dir, and can be downloaded per (session, turn). Decompression is streamed under a hard output cap.
enum_values: cc_session_id required when more than one row matches

groups.name: Distilling a finished session into durable memory (Step 1c summarization)

capabilities.name: LLM distillation of one transcript into a SessionSummary
capabilities.description: parse_transcript -> build_actions_view -> BAML b.Summarize (GCPFlash) -> host fills provenance -> apply_grounding. The host OVERWRITES the model's chat_session_id / claude_session_id / transcript_path / transcript_line_count / turn_count / chat_model / writer / summary_model / schema_version / generated_at after the call, so the model cannot forge provenance.

capabilities.name: Deterministic actions-only fallback when the summarizer fails
capabilities.description: ANY exception in the summarize path (BAML down, validation error, import failure) is caught and degrades to build_fallback_summary, which walks tool_use blocks and emits one MemoryItem per tool call. A session is never left un-remembered.

capabilities.name: MemoryItem category and confidence closed value sets
capabilities.description: Six categories and three confidence levels, defined in BAML with lowercase aliases and consumed by the renderer's ordering tables.

capabilities.name: Host-side quote grounding — unverified items are flagged, never dropped
capabilities.description: Every EvidenceRef's `verified` bool is recomputed host-side by substring-matching the quote against raw transcript lines [line_start, line_end] (1-based). The model is instructed to always emit verified=false. Items whose quotes do not check out are KEPT and flagged (SPEC-1c §4), so a hallucinated takeaway is visible rather than silently authoritative.

capabilities.name: Numbered actions view + shared tool classifier
capabilities.description: The summarizer is fed a line-numbered 'L<n> <kind>: <detail>' rendering of the transcript, not raw JSON. classify_tool_use is the ONE classifier shared by 1c memory and the Step-3 CCTrace so the two can never drift. Tool outputs are truncated at cfg.truncate_chars with the literal suffix '…[truncated]'.

capabilities.name: Change detection: only re-summarize a transcript that actually changed
capabilities.description: fingerprint(raw) = {line_count, sha256 hex}. is_changed compares against extra_state['summary_fingerprint']; no prior fingerprint counts as changed. This is what makes both the per-turn sync summarize and the Celery sweep idempotent.

capabilities.name: Where a distilled summary is written (tier + keys)
capabilities.description: The summary is persisted on the SUMMARIZED session's own ChatSession.extra_state under two keys — 'summary' (the SessionSummary dict) and 'summary_fingerprint' — via a single-key read-modify-write that must not clobber siblings. It is NOT written to results_history and NOT to the CCSessionTranscript table.

capabilities.name: Exactly one session is summarized synchronously per CC turn
capabilities.description: select_sync_target picks THE single most-recent CHANGED non-current session, so a turn pays for at most one Summarize call regardless of how many stale sessions the user has. Everything else is left to the Celery sweep.

groups.name: Injecting cross-session memory into a Container-CC turn

capabilities.name: Recency window over the user's OWN other sessions
capabilities.description: select_window takes the `window_size` most-recent sessions by updated_at, excluding the current chat. _session_metas restricts the candidate set to ChatSession.objects.filter(user=user) — never another user's sessions — and skips sessions with no resolvable project dirname. It defers the results_history column because including that multi-MB JSON in the ORDER BY filesort trips MySQL errno 1038.

capabilities.name: Deterministic memory markdown (no clock, no randomness)
capabilities.description: render_memory produces the user-tier CLAUDE.md body: a fixed header ('# Cross-session memory (auto-generated — do not edit)'), items grouped by category in _CATEGORY_ORDER and sorted within a category by confidence then session recency, then a '## Recent session transcripts (read-only, on-demand)' block listing one `<mount>/<sid>.jsonl — <gist>` line per window session. Output is a pure function of its inputs.

capabilities.name: fresh_session — clean-room turn with the memory layer disabled

capabilities.name: Read-only raw-transcript staging for on-demand depth

The dir is mounted read_only at /home/user/.cc-memory/transcripts — deliberately outside .claude so it can never collide with the session store or --resume.

capabilities.name: Cross-session memory tuning knobs (env-overridable)

CC entries (mode=='cc'), unrelated turns, error turns and bundle-less entries contribute NOTHING. CC replies are whitespace-collapsed and clipped at 200 chars with a '…'. Either section may be empty.

This direction carries STRUCTURE, not just prose.

groups.name: Durable transcript storage, recovery, and (non-)redaction

capabilities.name: zstd transcript blob per (chat_session, cc_session_id, turn_id)
capabilities.description: After a successful CC turn the raw .jsonl is zstd-compressed (level 10) and written to the CCSessionTranscript table via update_or_create, keyed by (chat_session, cc_session_id, turn_id) where turn_id is the run UUID. It lives in its OWN table, not extra_state, so hot ChatSession reads never load it (SPEC-3 §7/E6). uncompressed_size records the pre-compression byte count. There is no retention/pruning job.

capabilities.name: Decompression bomb guard on read
capabilities.description: decompress streams in 1MB chunks and raises TranscriptTooLarge once the accumulated output exceeds max_bytes (default 256MB; the endpoint uses settings.CC_TRANSCRIPT_MAX_BYTES with the same default), so a corrupted or hostile row cannot exhaust memory.

capabilities.name: Operator transcript recovery endpoint
capabilities.description: GET /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/transcript/{session}/{turn}/ streams the decompressed jsonl as application/x-ndjson with a transcript-{turn}.jsonl attachment name. Ownership is enforced (session filtered by request.user). When several rows share a turn_id and no cc_session_id query param is given it returns 400 'cc_session_id required'; otherwise the newest by created_at wins.

capabilities.name: Transcripts are stored UNREDACTED — the only redaction is env-for-logging
capabilities.description: Nothing filters the .jsonl before it is copied to output/raw/, compressed into the DB, staged for cross-session memory, or fed to the summarizer. The single redaction primitive in this subsystem is _redact_env, which masks 9 secret-bearing keys for operational log lines only. A test family must pin this rather than assume redaction exists.

capabilities.name: Per-turn raw transcript copy into the user's output tree
capabilities.description: run_cc_turn locates the newest *.jsonl under {cc_state_mnt}/projects with mtime >= turn_start-1, retrying up to 3 times with 0.2s sleeps (the file is written asynchronously by claude), and copies it to {output_mnt}/raw/transcript-{run_id}.jsonl. The basename is guarded by _safe_relpath before the copy.

capabilities.name: CC_PERSIST_STRICT — fail loudly vs deliver-anyway when persistence breaks
capabilities.description: If the transcript jsonl cannot be found after a successful turn, or on_turn_complete raises, the default behavior is to LOG and still deliver the reply (memory for that turn is lost silently). With settings.CC_PERSIST_STRICT=True (default False) it re-raises, converting the silent memory loss into a query_error.

groups.name: What a turn's memory activity looks like from outside

capabilities.name: Every CC turn terminates with exactly one query_complete or query_error
capabilities.description: The terminal frame is DEFERRED until after the staging sweep and artifact publish so the reply can report host-side artifact paths (D19). finalize() is a safety net emitting query_complete with reply '(no response)' when the stream ended without a result frame. A non-success result subtype or is_error becomes query_error.

capabilities.name: The four on-disk artifacts that prove memory ran for a turn
capabilities.description: A test can assert memory end-to-end without entering the container: the rendered {memory_mnt}/CLAUDE.md, its copy at {cc_state_mnt}/CLAUDE.md, the staged {memory_mnt}/transcripts/<sid>.jsonl set, and {output_mnt}/raw/transcript-<run_id>.jsonl. All four live under DMAC_USER_ROOT_MOUNT (/dmac/users) inside the nextseek container.

capabilities.name: The recall/query manifest a CC op prints to stdout
capabilities.description: nextseek-recall and nextseek-query emit a single JSON manifest line: {turn_id, bundle_id, total, row_count, columns, path} (query also carries reply, and returns turn_id=None). The `path` is the scratch file the agent then reads, which is how raw NS rows physically cross the engine boundary.

families.description: Create, name, resume and rehydrate a session; act as the right user or refuse.

groups.name: Keep, name and provision my session

capabilities.name: Persistent session state backends (SQLite or MySQL)
capabilities.description: Session values are JSON-serialized into a session_state(session_id, key, value) table with upsert semantics; placeholder style is translated so the same SQL text works on both backends.

capabilities.name: Per-project / per-user provisioning with fail-closed project resolution
capabilities.description: Each user's CC tree lives at {project}/{user}/ inside one named volume. The SEEK project is resolved with the user's own credentials; empty membership becomes an isolated personal namespace and any unresolved state rejects the turn rather than guessing.
enum_values: dir kinds: input, shared, scratch, output, cc-state/<session>, _memory/<session>, _memory/<session>/transcripts
shared_subpath deliberately omits the user segment (project-scoped)
refusal: 'Your SEEK project membership changed for this chat. Please start a new chat.'

capabilities.name: Automatic chat titling on every route
capabilities.description: Every turn that reaches the end of dispatch titles the chat if it has none, using this turn's query as fallback, so CC and out-of-scope turns no longer leave a chat stuck on 'New chat'.
enum_values: fallback title source: this turn's query (CC / unrelated turns populate no results_history)

groups.name: Act as the right user, or refuse

capabilities.name: Per-turn identity gate with fail-closed impersonation refusal
capabilities.description: Every entry point binds the turn to the asking user's credentials by shallow-copying the config. A request-scoped caller supplying an incomplete pair is REFUSED with a user-facing explanation instead of silently running as the service account; single-operator surfaces (no credentials mapping) warn and proceed.
enum_values: consequence: DRF TOKEN callers are refused

capabilities.name: Admin-only controls
capabilities.description: Three privileges are admin-gated and silently downgraded for everyone else: forcing a route, raising the per-turn wall-clock, and the whole evaluator REST surface.

capabilities.name: Credential brokering: the agent holds only the user's NExtSEEK login
capabilities.description: Nine of the thirteen CC ops run server-side in the sidecar; the agent sends {op, args, ns_login, request_id} over a WebSocket and never holds database or provider credentials. An empty api_user is rejected so identities cannot collapse onto one shared staging dir.
enum_values: sidecar ops (9): entity, parse, api-read, api-write, graph, report, generate-submission, run-ls, build-upload-xlsx
viewset ops (4, bypass the sidecar and its write gate): query, plan, pipeline, recall
ws max_size 16 MiB (1 MiB default truncated large responses into a WS 1009 close)

groups.name: Session persistence, CC resume, and chat rehydration

capabilities.name: Sniffing and persisting Claude Code's own session id
capabilities.description: make_session_sniffer wraps send_event: the first time an emitted event's data carries a truthy cc_session_id different from the last seen, it invokes on_session_id BEFORE forwarding (last-wins, deduped). The service persists it as extra_state['cc_session_id'] via a single-key merge. It is deliberately surfaced as cc_session_id and NOT session_id — leaking it as session_id caused a multi-turn 404 when the frontend promoted it as the active chat.

capabilities.name: --resume is only passed when a transcript actually exists on disk
capabilities.description: store_has_transcripts globs {cc_state_dir}/projects/**/*.jsonl. When a resume id is stored but the store is empty (turn 1, or a wiped volume), effective_session_id is set to None and the turn starts fresh with a log line 'cc: resume id present but store empty; starting fresh' — claude never tries to resume a session whose transcript is gone.

capabilities.name: Per-chat .claude state store mounted across ephemeral containers
capabilities.description: build_user_dirs derives cc_state_subpath = '{project}/{user}/cc-state/{session_id}', mounted RW at /home/user/.claude so transcripts persist across the one-container-per-turn model. Every segment (project dirname, user_id, session_id) is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]{1,128}$ and rejected if '.', '..', contains '/' or NUL, before any interpolation. Backing dirs are mkdir'd + chmod 0777 by Django and a missing subpath is fail-closed BEFORE spawn (the Engine refuses to start otherwise).

capabilities.name: Which chat a request lands in (session_id / force_new / most-recent reuse)
capabilities.description: _resolve_session: an explicit session_id is looked up scoped to request.user (a foreign id raises DoesNotExist → 404 'Session not found or you do not own it'); force_new=true always creates; otherwise the most recently updated session of that user is reused, and one is created if none exists. Reusing the most-recent session is what makes an unscoped request inherit a prior chat's memory.

capabilities.name: Rehydrating a chat in the UI (GET session ?include=turns)
capabilities.description: When chat_log exists it is the source of truth: each entry with a user_query becomes a Turn, reply resolved as assistant_reply > bundle.terminal_reply/reply > assistant_reply_preview, artifacts from the entry or extracted from the bundle, plus cc_traces. True non-answer entries (unrelated / error, no reply and no bundle) are HIDDEN. With no chat_log it falls back to projecting results_history bundles — which is why a CC-only legacy chat rehydrates empty.

capabilities.name: A chat is pinned to the SEEK project it started in
capabilities.description: The first CC turn stores extra_state['cc_project_dirname']. Every later turn re-resolves the user's project and, if the resolved dirname differs, REFUSES the turn with 'Your SEEK project membership changed for this chat. Please start a new chat.' rather than silently relocating the chat's memory/scratch tree to a different project subpath. Project resolution failure is also fail-closed.

capabilities.name: Deleting a chat drops its DB memory but not the on-disk store
capabilities.description: DELETE session removes the ChatSession row (cascading CCSessionTranscript rows and with them chat_log / cc_traces / summary / cc_session_id). The volume-backed cc-state transcripts and _memory/<session>/ staging dirs under dmac-cc-users are NOT removed. A deleted session also stops contributing to the cross-session window because _session_metas iterates ChatSession rows.

groups.name: Concurrency and integrity of the memory writes themselves

capabilities.name: refresh-then-merge on every extra_state single-key write
capabilities.description: _merge_extra_state does session.refresh_from_db(fields=['extra_state']) BEFORE merging, because the ChatSession object is loaded at turn start while a nested request on the same session (a different ORM object) can seed keys mid-turn — without the reload, writing cc_session_id would erase a concurrently-seeded pipeline_agent key that the router gate reads next turn. _append_cc_turn_complete does the same.

capabilities.name: DictSessionAdapter.save — row-locked merge for bundles, whole-column overwrite for extra_state
capabilities.description: save() takes select_for_update on the row and merges results_history BY BUNDLE ID (this turn's version wins on conflict) so two concurrent turns cannot erase each other's bundles. extra_state, however, is written as the whole cache minus the typed keys, snapshotted at adapter construction — so it does NOT get the same protection. On a backend without row locking the whole thing falls through to a plain save.

capabilities.name: FIFO eviction keeps the NEWEST entries
capabilities.description: append_capped returns a NEW list keeping only the last `cap` entries. Newest-kept is load-bearing: a chat_log[:cap] (keep-oldest) mutation must fail the pinned test. Applied identically to chat_log and to the cc_traces mirror, both capped at MAX_CC_CHAT_LOG_TURNS=50.

capabilities.name: The cc_traces mirror is written in the same shot as chat_log
capabilities.description: apply_turn_to_extra_state appends to BOTH extra_state['chat_log'] and the locked SPEC-3 §6.5 extra_state['cc_traces'] mirror in ONE pure transform, both FIFO-capped so the mirror stays small (it is loaded on every session read). Each trace carries schema_version '3/trace-v1', ordered steps with kind/tool/detail/status/action, a tools_used tally, files_created/modified, and num_turns/duration_ms/cost_usd from the terminal result frame.
enum_values: Step.kind: bash | write | edit | read | skill | tool | text

families.description: Timeout, budget cap, max turns, the error taxonomy and failover.

groups.name: Fail safely: error taxonomy, repair and failover

capabilities.name: CC structured error code taxonomy with fixed exit codes
capabilities.description: Every CC op failure emits a one-line JSON error to stderr with a stable code and exit status, and SKILL.md documents the correct agent response for each. The authoritative dict lives in the sidecar contract.
enum_values: RECALL_FAILED (5) — emitted by nextseek-recall but absent from ERROR_EXIT and the SKILL.md table

capabilities.name: LLM failure classification and per-call ledger
capabilities.description: Every structured LLM call is classified into one of five outcomes and written to a ledger with latency, tokens, retry count and stop reason; the classification decides whether the run retries, backs off, fails over or dies.
enum_values: outcome: throttle (429 -> backoff then retry, then LLMFatalError)

ledger fields: agent, provider, model, attempt, outcome, elapsed_ms, timeout_seconds, thinking_budget, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, retry_attempts, bedrock_latency_ms, request_id, stop_reason, error

capabilities.name: Cross-provider failover on 503
capabilities.description: When an agent's provider returns 503 the call is retried against an ordered chain of alternate model profiles, skipping any whose credentials are absent; an exhausted chain raises LLMFatalError('All provider fallbacks exhausted').

capabilities.name: Structured-output repair loop
capabilities.description: Parses model text into the target Pydantic model and on validation failure feeds the errors plus raw output back for a corrected object, up to `retries` times. Provider quirks (code fences, single-element list wrapping) are normalized first.
enum_values: repair prompt: 'Your previous output did not validate for schema {model}. Validation errors: {errors}. Re-output ONLY a corrected JSON object…'

capabilities.name: Fatal LLM error containment
capabilities.description: An LLMFatalError anywhere in a turn is caught, reported as a readable reply, emitted as query_error with fatal=True, and recorded in chat memory as an error turn so the next turn sees no hole in history. LLMFatalError subclasses BaseException deliberately so it bypasses bare `except Exception` in agent code.
enum_values: reply: '**The request could not be completed.**'
run_query re-raises any non-fatal exception after emitting query_error; run_query_plan returns a readable error reply instead

groups.name: Bound the cost, the blast radius and the network

capabilities.name: Ephemeral sandboxed agent container per turn
capabilities.description: Each CC turn spawns one throwaway `claude` sibling container with private input read-only, project shared dir read-only, per-user read-write scratch and per-session Claude state — always terminating with exactly one query_complete or query_error after publishing.
enum_values: container name: dmac-cc-agent-<run_id> (409 stale-name force-remove retry)
_preflight_subpath_dirs fails closed if a backing dir is missing

capabilities.name: Per-turn cost, turn-count and wall-clock caps
capabilities.description: Every CC turn is bounded three ways, with a watchdog that stops and force-removes the container; admins can raise the wall-clock from the Debug panel but the server clamps to an env-bounded ceiling.
enum_values: overrun -> query_error reason 'exec_timeout': 'Container-CC turn exceeded the {n}s limit and was stopped.'

capabilities.name: De-credentialed agent environment (single-source env builder)
capabilities.description: One function is the sole source of the agent's environment so no secret can sneak in via an inline dict; the agent holds zero AWS credentials, reaching Bedrock only through an auth-proxy sidecar and NExtSEEK only as the authenticated user.
enum_values: set: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH=1, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1, NEXTSEEK_USERNAME/API_USER, NEXTSEEK_PASSWORD/API_PASS, AWS_REGION, NEXTSEEK_BASE_URL/URL, NEXTSEEK_SIDECAR_HOST/PORT, DMAC_PATH_MAPPINGS, NEXTSEEK_CHAT_SESSION_ID
redacted keys: NEXTSEEK_PASSWORD, API_PASS, DMAC_PATH_MAPPINGS, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, NEO4J_PASSWORD, MYSQL_PASSWORD, MYSQL_DEV_PASSWORD, GCP_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
agent rule: 'Never run bare env, printenv, or set'

capabilities.name: Segmented CC network with fail-fast availability check
capabilities.description: The agent joins a dedicated 2/3-node network rather than the shared stack network, so it has no L3 reach to neo4j or mysql. A missing daemon, image or network is reported as an unavailable route rather than auto-created.
enum_values: checks: daemon ping, image presence, network presence — never creates the network
failure: query_error 'Container-CC route is not available: <detail>'

capabilities.name: Auto-mode trusted-infrastructure descriptors
capabilities.description: Rather than disabling permissions, the engine passes a $defaults-FIRST auto-mode settings blob describing the lab's own trusted services so the classifier does not abort legitimate NExtSEEK calls. Only descriptors travel, never secret values.
enum_values: list MUST start with the literal $defaults so built-in trust is EXTENDED, not replaced
descriptor sources: NEXTSEEK_INTERNAL_BASE_URL / NEXTSEEK_BASE_URL / NEXTSEEK_URL, NEO4J_URI, GCP_API_KEY (presence only)

capabilities.name: Environment normalization in the shim and entrypoint
capabilities.description: Quote-stripping of every env var up front (docker --env-file preserves literal quotes), plus translation of the injected NEXTSEEK_* names into the API_* names the server pipeline expects, the GCP profile pin and the per-user outputs dir default.
enum_values: quote strip only when first and last chars are the same quote char and len >= 2
entrypoint scrubs the settings.local.json `env` block on every start

capabilities.name: Dry-run mode for wiring verification without credentials
capabilities.description: With NEXTSEEK_DRY_RUN=1 every op returns a minimal correctly-shaped JSON response without touching any LLM, REST or Neo4j call, and the credential precondition is skipped.

groups.name: Hard limits on a single turn (and the observable when each one trips)

capabilities.name: Per-turn wall-clock timeout (watchdog stop + force-remove)
capabilities.description: A daemon thread waits turn_timeout seconds on a done Event; on expiry it sets a _timed_out flag and calls container.stop(timeout=2) then container.remove(force=True), which ends the stdout stream so the read loop exits. Default 180s. NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS sets the default but is itself min()'d against NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_HARD_MAX (also 180), so raising the ceiling requires setting the HARD_MAX var.
enum_values: NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default = hard max, clamped to it)

capabilities.name: Admin per-request wall-clock override, clamped server-side
capabilities.description: QueryRequest.max_turn_length_s is honored ONLY for is_staff/is_superuser (mirroring the force_route / use_prod gate); non-admins always get the configured default. clamp_turn_timeout maps None/<=0 to the default and otherwise clamps into [30, NEXTSEEK_CC_TIMEOUT_HARD_MAX], so the Debug panel can never exceed what the deployment allows.

capabilities.name: Per-turn USD budget cap (claude --max-budget-usd)
capabilities.description: Default $0.50 via NEXTSEEK_CC_MAX_BUDGET_USD; a value of 0 (or falsey) OMITS the flag entirely, disabling the cap. Claude Code stops the turn when accrued cost hits the cap and emits a terminal `result` frame with a non-success subtype, which the translator converts to query_error. The turn's actual spend is surfaced on query_complete as total_cost_usd.

capabilities.name: Per-turn agent-loop cap (claude --max-turns)
capabilities.description: Default 50 agent turns inside ONE chat turn, via NEXTSEEK_CC_MAX_TURNS (passed through as a string, always present). Exhaustion surfaces the same way as the budget cap: a non-success terminal result → query_error. The consumed count is reported on query_complete as num_turns and copied into the CCTrace.

capabilities.name: The nested NExtSEEK turn's own 300s poll deadline inside a 180s CC turn
capabilities.description: When the agent runs nextseek-query, AssistantClient POSTs query/async and polls tasks/{id}/progress with a total deadline of 300s, a 30s per-request timeout and up to 4 retries per poll iteration on transport stalls. Exceeding it yields the sentinel 'stream ended without terminal event'. Because the CC turn's own wall-clock default is 180s, the outer watchdog normally kills the container FIRST — the 300s deadline is only reachable when the hard max has been raised.

capabilities.name: cc_turn_meta — the caps in force are streamed to the Debug panel
capabilities.description: Before spawning, the service emits a cc_turn_meta progress event carrying model_id, the resume cc_session_id (or null), budget_usd and the RESOLVED turn_timeout_s. This is the only place the effective per-turn caps are visible to a user.

capabilities.name: Request-level input cap
capabilities.description: QueryRequest.query is min_length=1, max_length=32000; violation is a 422 validation error before any routing or session work. Batch upload has a separate 200MB total cap (BATCH_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) returning 413.

capabilities.name: A killed turn still lands in memory as a non-answer entry
capabilities.description: wrap_send_event tracks terminal state (FIRST query_error wins); should_append_non_answer is true when an error was seen, no query_complete arrived, and the route was not 'unrelated'. The finally block then appends a chat_log entry with status='error', the error text, mode derived from router_choice, and NO assistant_reply — via the adapter when NS ran, or via a refresh-then-RMW on extra_state otherwise. This is why a timed-out CC turn does not make the chat sticky and does not appear in the rehydrated UI.

capabilities.name: Silent truncation caps applied to remembered text
capabilities.description: Memory is lossy by design at several fixed points; none of these raise, so an over-long value is quietly clipped. Enumerated here because a test that asserts on remembered text must know the exact boundary.
enum_values: router history 5 turns; user 512 B, reply 1024 B, error 256 B, uid 64 B, 3 uids
memory items 8 per session; window 10 sessions
memory_coder profile 50000 chars; computed result 60000 chars

capabilities.name: Degenerate-turn replies
capabilities.description: Four dead ends that still return a diagnosable reply rather than an error: search classified with no endpoint, API agent could not build a request, graph agent produced no Cypher, parser returned an unimplemented mode.
enum_values: 'The parser recognized this as a database search, but did not specify an endpoint.'
'The API Agent could not construct a valid request for this query.'
'Graph agent could not generate a query.'

capabilities.name: Planner halt decisions and termination reasons
capabilities.description: How and why a plan run ends: the planner may halt voluntarily, or the loop forces termination on a repeated strategy, exhausted budget, missing inputs, or a hard step failure.

capabilities.name: Per-step halt policy (StepOutcome)
capabilities.description: A plan step can declare that an empty result is fatal or that its own failure is survivable; the parser sets halt_on_empty for non-intersectable UID-producing searches so an empty set stops the plan instead of intersecting to zero.

capabilities.name: In-band plan self-assessment (plan_evaluator agent)
capabilities.description: The final step of every planner turn grades the run and prepends an **Evaluator** block to the reply. Distinct from the out-of-band evaluator subsystem (SYS-EVAL) despite sharing the name.
enum_values: other fields: answered_query, execution_consistent, reason, what_went_wrong, user_safe_summary, confidence

capabilities.name: Pipeline wizard turn outcomes, cancel words and budgets
capabilities.description: Each wizard turn returns exactly one action; a short deterministic cancel-word list abandons a build without consulting the model, and a 12-iteration tool budget ends a runaway turn by asking the user how to proceed.
enum_values: cancel tokens: any message starting with /cancel
MAX_ITER = 12 -> "I couldn't finish within my step budget. Tell me how to proceed, or say 'cancel'."

capabilities.name: Wizard session state and chat-log snapshot
capabilities.description: The wizard has no state machine: the transcript itself is the state, alongside resolved refs and emitted artifact paths, with a compact snapshot written to the chat log each turn.
enum_values: state keys: active, messages, resolved{uids,accessions}, artifacts{cohorts,samplesheet,base_dir,excluded_accessions,params,launch,luria_runs}, pipeline_key, accession_file_paths, detected_species, bundle_key, launch_plan

groups.name: Watch the turn happen live and reconstruct it later

capabilities.name: Live per-agent progress event stream (NS)
capabilities.description: The orchestrator emits structured events through an injected send_event callback so a UI can show a live agent stepper; a None callback is a no-op.
enum_values: agent labels: catalog, entity, parser, memory, reporter, report_writer, system, graph, chatter, api, planner, evaluator, pipeline_agent

capabilities.name: Claude stream-json translated into the same event vocabulary (CC)
capabilities.description: The agent's native stream is translated into the six frontend events: tool calls become start/complete search steps, narration and thinking become instantaneous steps, and the result becomes one query_complete carrying Claude's own accrued cost.
enum_values: frontend events: agent_started, agent_complete, search_started, search_complete, query_complete, query_error
extra debug events from the service layer: route_decided, cc_turn_meta
tool detail keys: bash->command, read/write/edit/multiedit->file_path, notebookedit->notebook_path, glob/grep->pattern, webfetch->url, websearch->query, task->description
terminal frame carries total_cost_usd, num_turns, duration_ms

capabilities.name: Per-turn CC activity trace for the Debug panel
capabilities.description: One trace per chat turn assembled from three never-conflated sources: ordered transcript tool steps, the headless result frame's meta, and the authoritative scratch diff.
enum_values: Step.kind: bash, write, edit, read, skill, tool, text
CCTrace fields: cc_session_id, ts, transcript_line_count, turn_count, num_turns, duration_ms, cost_usd, steps, tools_used, files_created, files_modified

capabilities.name: Per-turn REST, LLM and prompt ledgers
capabilities.description: Three append-only JSONL ledgers per turn — one REST call record with full result payload, one LLM-call record with latency/tokens/outcome, and one prompt record per agent stage. All no-op silently without a path; instrumentation never breaks the request path.

capabilities.name: Streamlit live step tracker labels
capabilities.description: The standalone UI maps the shared event vocabulary onto human labels for its st.status stepper.

groups.name: Turn delivery: submit, stream, poll

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/query/async/ (the routed chat entry point)
capabilities.description: The endpoint the chat UI actually posts to. Validates QueryRequest, resolves the session, creates a QueryTask(status='running'), spawns a daemon thread, and returns HTTP 202 {task_id, session_id} immediately. Routing (RG-1..RG-4) happens inside the worker, so a routing outcome is only observable via the progress stream, never in the HTTP response.

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/cc/query/async/ (force Container-CC)
capabilities.description: Identical envelope and response to RG-8.1 but calls _start_task(force_cc=True), skipping the router. Not exercised by the frontend; used by harnesses and operators.

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/assistant/query/ (SSE streaming, NS-only)
capabilities.description:
The pre-router streaming entry point. Runs chat_nextseek in a thread feeding a queue.Queue, and streams 'event: <type>
data: <json>

' frames with Cache-Control no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering no. No router is consulted — this endpoint always runs the NExtSEEK engine, and it honors only mode 'plan' vs default. A None sentinel closes the stream.

capabilities.name: POST /nextseek_api/assistant/query/async/ (async, NS-only, has the pipeline mode)
capabilities.description: Same async shape as RG-8.1 but no router: always the NExtSEEK engine, with the three-way mode dispatch (plan / pipeline / standard). This is the only endpoint that reaches run_pipeline_launch.

capabilities.name: GET tasks/{task_id}/progress/ (poll fallback, both viewsets)
capabilities.description: The same response shape is served at TWO paths: /nextseek_api/assistant/tasks/{task_id}/progress/ and /nextseek_api/cc-assistant/tasks/{task_id}/progress/. Both filter by task_id AND request.user (404 otherwise) and both suppress `result` until the task is terminal. The frontend uses this only when the websocket fails to open.
enum_values: response fields: task_id, session_id, status, progress[], result?
result present only when status in (completed, error)
404: "Task not found or you do not own it."

capabilities.name: WS ws/assistant/progress/{task_id}/ (primary transport)
capabilities.description: The single existing consumer both engines stream through, so chat_frontend needs no per-route code. Polls QueryTask every 300 ms, pushes new events, sends a final `done` frame at a terminal status and closes. Requires an authenticated user AND ownership — the task UUID is explicitly not a capability token. Browser WS cannot send Authorization headers, so Basic/Token-only clients are anonymous here and must fall back to RG-8.5. Origin is checked against CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS + CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS (a missing Origin header is allowed).

capabilities.name: QueryTask status machine and event persistence
